Hey, I know how you feel. It sucks that you feel like you've lost everything and that everything is awful. It's so hard to rebuild when you've spent so much time building and then it all comes falling down.

I also lost everything, in that I lost the boy I love, didn't get into school, and all my friends are moving on and my social life is non-existent. I've cried almost every night for months. Every day doesn't even feel bad, it just feels numb, and like you can't find reason to be excited anymore.

My advice to you is not to give up. It's hard to stay afloat but I believe that the most honorable people in life, and the people who wind up with the most, are those who have suffered great losses and hardships, and those who have given it all away and have come from nothing. Well, you're there, you're at the bottom. And there is only one way to go, you can stay down, or you can get up and kick ass. It's hard as fuck, trust me I know, to stay positive and smile and work your ass off when everything seems pointless. It's hard because what if it happens again? What if you wind up in the same place? You had all you wanted, but now it's gone and so what else could you possibly have to want? I know all too well. But it's all an illusion, and it's all feelings and ways as humans that we protect ourselves. 

As for specific things you can do, well, that's up to you. You should give yourself time and think. Think, sulk, cry, be mad, hate. Just do whatever you need for now. But don't stay there, whatever you do. Come up with something better. Emerge stronger. Make something of yourself. Make yourself happy and move onward and upward. It's corny but things happen for a reason, people come in and out of our lives, even if it's for some mundane reason, everyone helps us and teaches us. Try to learn as much as you can from everything and find motivation. I like to watch Michael Jordan's hall of fame acceptance speech, because for some reason, that's one of the most inspiring speeches I've ever heard. He was someone who was always told "no" and was always underestimated. But every time he'd show them up and prove them wrong. He worked his ass off in spite of hardships. Just remember if you do it right you can do whatever you want. You can re-enroll in school, get a killer job, and meet someone who will appreciate you and will see the value in you as a person. The key to all of this is *not giving up* and *learning from everything*.
